note: The Piast Polish kings competed with the Teutonic Order for control of Pomerania and later Samogitia (Lithuanian territory claimed by the Order) throughout the 13th–14th centuries. Władysław I 'the Short' unified fragmented Poland (1320) and immediately challenged the Order, winning the famous lawsuit at the papal court of Avignon (1320–1321) that granted Poland reparations — never collected. The Piast conflict with the Order established the territorial claims that the Jagiellonians later enforced militarily. The loss of Danzig/Gdańsk to the Order (1308) was the grievance that drove Polish policy toward the Order for 150 years.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Piast-Teutonic conflict establishes the territorial claims (Pomerania, Danzig, the Vistula corridor) that define Polish-German tension for 600 years; the papal lawsuit shows that legal strategies against the Order could be pursued even when military strength was insufficient
